meta.title: Dutch Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 918 expressions · 306 everyday, 543 idioms, 69 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 918 Dutch set phrases, idioms and proverbs, in three subdecks: 306 everyday phrases, 543 idioms and 69 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Dutch → English (see the Dutch, recall the meaning) and English → Dutch (see an English meaning, recall the Dutch) — each with a schedule of its own. This is a companion to the five level decks, Dutch A1 to C1, and not one of them: a level is a list of words, and an expression is a unit a list of words cannot see. Nothing here is taught by any of the five, so the two can be studied together without repeating an entry. The PHRASES are the expressions Wiktionary files as phrases and does not mark as idiomatic — mostly the everyday formulas a Dutch speaker uses as one piece (weet je, wat een, het spijt me …), with the greetings for the holidays and some sayings Wiktionary files the same way. The IDIOMS are expressions whose meaning is not their words' (van plan zijn, zorgen maken, in de buurt …), and the PROVERBS the sayings Wiktionary files as proverbs (te mooi om waar te zijn, de tijd zal het leren, kleren maken de man …). Only expressions made of Dutch words are here: the Latin and French tags Dutch writing borrows (in vitro, mea culpa) are left out. Within each subdeck the expressions come in the order of how many of Tatoeba's Dutch sentences contain them — an expression that is a verb being counted with its verb in any form and in either place, since a Dutch main clause moves the verb away from the rest (in de war zijn: ik ben helemaal in de war) — and only 344 of the 918 are found there at all; the rest follow in the order of how common their words are in film and television subtitles. Every expression has Wiktionary's pronunciation beneath it where Wiktionary gives one. Real example sentences come with 344 of the 918 expressions, three apiece for 167, with the expression picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Expressions, meanings, pronunciation and the idiom and proverb labels: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Order: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR, then a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba, CC BY 2.0 FR.
